name: Amiga 1200
description: Commodore's last mass-market Amiga, released in October 1992. It brought the AGA chipset and a 32-bit 68EC020 to the familiar wedge-shaped home computer, with 256-colour screens and an internal IDE hard-drive port. Commodore went bankrupt in 1994, cutting its life short.

specs.graphics: AGA: 256 colours from 16.8 million, HAM8 mode up to 262,144

curiosities: The Amiga CD32 console was built on essentially the same AGA hardware.
It has a PCMCIA Type II slot on its side, used for RAM cards and network adapters.
After Commodore's 1994 bankruptcy, the German company Escom bought the Amiga rights and put the A1200 back into production.
Its HAM8 mode can show up to 262,144 colours on screen at once.
